chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
editorText:
“Well! First thing first, back to where we began” the teacher insisted politely. “This morning we will be carrying out a deep space airlock exercise. I hope you’re all prepared for the rapid decompression of the chamber.” At a sudden instance all the bulk head doors to the class room closed tight, dead bolting into the ships frame creating an airtight seal.

“Please note! Any loose items are to be declared now, unless you want it coming back as a missile and putting a hole in you or your friend a few years later” A silent tension overwhelmed the room, the students sat waiting in silent anticipation. One of the students intervened for a moment, “Are these methods not unorthodox, how are we supposed to learn if we are stressed”, “Well” Responded the teacher, “If you cannot operate under stress, then how can you be expected to operate in the real world when things go sideways?” A sudden prang was heard followed by a sharp hissing sound. Air escaped the room at a rapid rate. The students felt their ear drums lightly expand as the room pressure dropped slowly with increasing intensity.

 In that instant an alarm sounded through the room. “Failure to deploy oxygen masks, please resort to manual donning of masks.” At this moment, the teacher had quickly taken a seat and gone into a meditative state, he did not breathe, but observed silently as the students around him scattered.

One of Shai’s personal paper notes was sucked straight from her uniform pocket fluttering rapidly to the vacuum hole being succeed out into space through a tiny mechanical hole.

The moment one of the students passed out on the ground, he rose from his seated position, grabbed one of the manual oxygen donning masks and placed it over the student’s mouth. At this time all the students have watched the teacher, grabbed the oxygen masks in the roof holds and placed them around their heads taking in deep breaths of relief. At this moment the air lock has re-engaged and the hole had been mechanically re-sealed. The engineering and thought that had gone into the mechanism was apparent.

The teacher, without even needing to don a mask, rose to his feet almost as if nothing had occurred. “Now how many of you believed in this instant you were going to Die?” with this the room fell silent. Slowly one by one all of the hands began to raise. All except one at the end of the table; John. He hadn’t raised his hand almost as if to draw attention to himself. John had observed quickly when the airlock initially failed, he noted above him a small latch where the oxygen mask had been contained. He pulled down the latch where an oxygen kit appeared. He placed the first kit on himself, then continued to grab another and assist his partner Tau, regulating her intake to compensate with the vacuum.

Satisfied with the results and the students, the teacher gave an affirming nod, as if to say “Well you have all passed this test” with that he continued. “It is important that we are able to work under stress, that we collect ourselves. To remain calm in any and all emergencies, the latter is death. If we cannot do this then we will not survive. That is why! This training will push you to your extremes, so that you are ready for the event before it even occurs. We are here to prepare you, we are here to ensure you survive, to ensure you are competent and have the both the physical and technical skills to thrive calmly in such a way that you may have time to assist your shipmates should they lose their way”

"Now!" said the instructor. “I will have your captain take the floor to introduce you to your new suits; I am sure, as you all know, you are in capable hands.” John bowed his head to the instructor ever so lightly, then rose to his feet and began walking decisively around the horseshoe table and his colleagues toward the instructor's position before the class at the other end of the room.
